subject: Request: interactive tail-latency heatmap by model-variant & tenant
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.io>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.io>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.io>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: interactive tail-latency heatmap by model-variant & tenant

Hi team,

Quick ask from a recent customer engagement with Acme (copied below): they had a hard incident where multi-tenant tail-latency spiked only when a particular LLM variant (quantized-gpt-small) served a specific tenant slice. The current console gives per-route percentiles and a token-cost breakdown, but we couldn't quickly surface "which model variant + tenant pair is driving the 99.9th% tail" over a rolling week.

Proposal (MVP):
- An interactive heatmap in Console under Observability -> Paths that maps: rows = model variant, cols = tenant (or tenant group), color = 99th/99.9th latency.
- Time-range selector (last 1h/24h/7d) + sample-rate control (full / 10% / 1%); allow zooming into the underlying traces.
- Click into a cell to open a pre-populated forensic query and a short list of recent high-cost token flows for that pairing.

Why this matters:
- Faster ops -> shorter MTTR for SLO breaches driven by model changes or tenant behavior.
- Helps product & sales precisely place mitigation (pin variant, add prefix cache, throttle tenant) and quantify cost impact.

Ask from you all:
1) Marissa — does this fit a product/Console priority we can slot for Q4 roadmap exploration?
2) Dylan — infra feasibility: can we materialize the variant+tenant time-series with acceptable ingest overhead and sampling gates, or do we need a lightweight aggregator?
3) Stephanie/Ben — UX/engineering cost estimate for a first-pass interactive tile and drill flow (basic heatmap + link to traces).

Attachments: I attached a quick mock (tail-heatmap-prototype.png) and a small sample query set I used with Acme (sample-query-set.csv).

Thanks — happy to sketch this in the next observability sync.

— Olga
Olga Petrov | Senior Solutions Engineer

Subject: Re: Request: interactive tail-latency heatmap by model-variant & tenant

Thanks, Olga — great concrete ask and useful mock. High level thoughts:

- Product fit: this maps to our "route diagnostics" theme but is different enough that it could be an incremental Console tile rather than a full-blown new page. I'd prefer a phased approach:
  * Phase 1 (MVP): static heatmap snapshot + cell drill -> launches a runbook + pre-populated trace query.
  * Phase 2: interactive time-series layering + linked anomaly detection.

- Priority: I can carve a discovery spike in late September (2 sprints) to validate backend needs and UX wireframes. If discovery is promising, we'll propose a Q4 experiment.

Open Qs for infra:
- What cardinality do you expect for "tenant" (tenants vs slices vs org)? Can we limit to top-200 active tenants by tokens/day to keep matrix size reasonable?
- Do we need separate heatmaps for embeddings/generation vs chat?

I'll add this to our product sync and tag INFRA-1723.

—Marissa
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.io>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.io>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.io>
Date: 2027-09-15T02:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: interactive tail-latency heatmap by model-variant & tenant

Short answer: feasible, but with tradeoffs.

Notes from infra POV:
- Cardinality & rollup: limiting to top-N tenants (by tokens/day) is the right approach. For an MVP we should do top-128 tenants and top-12 variants. That yields a 12x128 matrix — acceptable.
- Data model: we can emit (timestamp, variant_id, tenant_id, p50/p95/p99/p999) at a fixed aggregation interval (1m or 5m). That reduces raw ingest vs per-request telemetry.
- Sampling: enable adaptive sampling: full collection when alerting is happening, otherwise reservoir sampling at the edge (1% with uplifts for outliers).
- Storage: use existing metrics index (cost neutral) for the aggregated time-series; keep raw traces for 7d.

Implications: we need a small agent-side change to tag the model variant consistently and a backend job (batch) to emit the aggregated rows. I estimate a 3 week infra spike + 2 week follow-on to harden.

I'll spin up a spike branch and link INFRA-1723. If product wants discovery next week, we can demo a static SVG heatmap backed by precomputed CSVs.

—Dylan
Staff Infra Engineer
